content: Aum Namah Shivaya! Wishing all a great spiritual experience on the occasion of Maha Shiva Ratri!! One of the interesting things that we see in the images & idols of Shiva is the Kamandal (water pot) that he carries, containing Theertha (sacred water). As per the Puranas (Hindu Scriptures), the kamandal is made of copper or its alloys, and it is not only Shiva but also all the Rishis (sages) used to carry Kamandal with them for the same purpose. The divine power of Shiva and sages will definitely make the water in Kamandal very powerful. In addition, copper’s extraordinary ability to keep the water clean & microbe-free is something which we need to acknowledge. This knowledge is also highlighted in Ayurveda texts with a recommendation to store water in copper vessels. As an illustration, even today, we can see large copper vessels being used in Shiva temple at Rameswaram to store water from the sacred rivers.Does science approve this? Researchers from the University of Southampton and FRLHT, Bengaluru, have done a detailed study on this and have demonstrated the efficacy of copper against harmful bacteria like E. coli and Salmonella (waterborne bacteria), in contrast to stainless steel which supports the growth of microbes.From the sacred precincts of ancient Egypt to the mystical lands of Mesopotamia, copper artifacts adorned the sacred rituals. The ritualistic act of tossing copper coins into wells & ponds must also be adding to self-cleaning of water in these water bodies.Amidst the cosmic dance of Shiva on Maha Shiva Ratri, let us contemplate copper’s amazing power of making water – Pure & Powerful!
